clare_sales: Quick blocker for Nimbus POCCustomer says SSO keeps redirecting to an error page and SCIM provisioning intermittently gets 401. Theyre stuck in the pilot.

omar_se: Can you share the exact error page text/screens? Is the SAML ACS URL we provided matching the app config in their IdP?

clare_sales: Screenshot says: "We're sorry, something went wrong" after Okta redirects back. Their app shows ACS = https://private.nimbus.redwood-company.com/saml/acs but our logs show ACS reached is https://sso.redwood-inference.com/saml/acs/tn-019 (hosted). Looks like IdP is sending our hosted ACS even though their app is configured for private.

lee_prod: That usually happens when Okta uses the app-level Default RelayState or if they clicked a bookmarked link to the hosted entrypoint. Which flow is this: SP-initiated or IdP-initiated?

clare_sales: IdP-initiated. They said users click the Okta tile.

omar_se: In IdP-initiated flows Okta uses the app's ACS that was set when the app was created. If they later updated the tenant to private but didn't update the Okta app settings, Okta will keep using the old ACS on the app record. Ask them to edit the app and set the ACS to the private URL or to set the RelayState to the tenant-specific ACS in the assignment.

clare_sales: Customer prefers private (no hosted callback). They updated their app but still see hosted ACS in logs. Any cache on our side?

lee_prod: We cache tenant SSO endpoints in the auth service for 5 minutes to avoid DB lookups. If they changed the Console setting moments ago we might still serve the old ACS for a short window. We can force a refresh for their tenant: Console -> Tenants -> Nimbus -> Actions -> Refresh SSO Cache. I'll do that now.

infra_bot: action: refreshed sso cache for tenant=nimbus at 15:02 UTC.

clare_sales: They tested again and still get error page. New log shows SAML response arrives at private ACS but assertion consumer code returns 400: "Invalid RelayState: mismatch".

omar_se: RelayState mismatch often means the IdP sent RelayState that doesn't match the InResponseTo stored at SP if SP-initiated flow expected. But since it's IdP-initiated there shouldn't be InResponseTo. Could the RelayState be pointing back to the hosted init endpoint? Check the value.

lee_prod: Log snippet: relayState=https%3A%2F%2Fsso.redwood-inference.com%2Fstart%3Ftenant%3Dtn-019 . So Okta is passing a hosted start URL as RelayState. We should accept RelayState that points to either hosted or tenant private start URL for IdP-initiated unless we have strict validation on the tenant. For POC we can relax validation with a feature flag.

clare_sales: They'll accept hosted RelayState but insist the final ACS be private. Is that doable?

omar_se: Yes. Implement quick fix: allow RelayState values that start with our known base domains (sso.redwood-inference.com OR private.<tenant>.redwood-company.com) and then redirect to the private tenant after successful assertion. Add tenant flag `saml.accept_known_relaystate_domains=true` default false. Patch is small and safe for a POC.

infra_bot: deploy: saml-relay-fix to canary succeeded at 15:28 UTC.

clare_sales: Also need to fix the SCIM 401s. Customer says provisioning succeeds sometimes but other times they get 401 with body: "token expired". Token issued TTL is 60s per our docs?

lee_prod: We currently issue short-lived SCIM bearer tokens for security (60s) when Okta does an initial provisioning push; they should be exchanged for a longer lived connector token. If their Okta connector isn't configured to refresh, the token will expire between list and push calls. What connector method are they using?

clare_sales: Using Okta's built-in Provisioning (SCIM) integration. They didn't map the connector to use a refresh flow.

omar_se: For POC quick workaround: we can accept tokens with TTL up to 5m if tenant.poc_relaxed_scim_token_ttl=true. That reduces security but unblocks pilot. In parallel ask them to configure connector to use the API key (long-lived) we provided and point Okta provisioning to use that.

infra_bot: feature toggle set: tenant=nimbus poc_relaxed_scim_token_ttl=true (applies to scim ingress validation) at 15:34 UTC.

clare_sales: Sent them a step-by-step to switch the Okta SCIM connector to use the API key: Console -> Tenants -> Nimbus -> Integrations -> SCIM -> Show API key. They updated connector to use API key and initial provisioning succeeded. They also confirmed SSO redirect now lands on private app and users can sign in.

lee_prod: Follow-up: we'll revert the token TTL relaxation after POC (scheduled). Also add to Dedicated onboarding doc: ensure Okta app ACS is aligned with tenant private ACS, document RelayState behaviors, and require SCIM connector use of long-lived API key or connector with refresh support.

clare_sales: Pricing/ops note: customer asked if private ACS + custom certs is included in POC or extra charge. I confirmed custom TLS for private host is covered for POC but if they want sustained Dedicated with custom egress/managed certs it'll be part of enterprise onboarding SOW.

customer_bot: Nimbus IT: Verified sign-in and user provisioning. Thanks team. :tada:

clare_sales: Closing thread. Will add checklist items to the POC playbook and ping on the deal. :white_check_mark:
